fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says, "So Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, received their inheritance." (Joshua 16:4) Two sons of Joseph, one inheritance. That's a lot of names to keep straight, and you kept them straight.

That's it. The text says, "But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer." (Joshua 16:10) Gezer was part of the border Ephraim received, and the Canaanites stayed living there among the Ephraimites. Some jobs get left half-done. I once left a whole batch of dough on the counter overnight and called it resting.

Phinehas is a fine name, friend, but he isn't in this verse. The priest in the scene is Eleazar. The text says the daughters "…approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders…" (Joshua 17:4) Easy to grab a priest name off the shelf like a wrong cookie cutter. Check the verse and Eleazar is right there.

That's right. The daughters say, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." (Joshua 17:4) They come in with the LORD's command already in hand. That's like showing up to the meeting with the paperwork already stamped. Nobody does that, and they did.

Yes, baker. The text says, "…the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh." (Joshua 17:6) The daughters of Zelophehad received an inheritance among Manasseh's sons, and Gilead belonged to the rest of those sons. It's the land beyond the Jordan, set apart from the ten shares mentioned in verse 5.

That's it. They say, "…all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel." (Joshua 17:16) They say it right after telling Joshua the hill country is not enough for them. I think they were feeling the size of the challenge. I know that feeling. It's me staring at a triple batch.

Gates, friend? Nice try, but no gates in this verse. The sons of Joseph say the Canaanites "…have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel." (Joshua 17:16) Iron chariots, rolling around the valley. Hold that picture and the word sticks.

Idols? I see where your mind went, but this verse is about hardware on wheels. The sons of Joseph say the Canaanites "…have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel." (Joshua 17:16) Iron chariots. Say it twice and it stays put.

You got it, baker. Joshua says, "Although the Canaanites have iron chariots and although they are strong, you can drive them out." (Joshua 17:18) He names the chariots and the strength right out loud, and he still says they can drive them out. Iron chariots on one side, and Joshua's word on the other.
